title: ASTRAL score pour Ischemic AVC
formula:

how_to_use.why:
- Peut fournir des informations complémentaires sur le devenir fonctionnel à moyen terme chez les patients ayant présenté un accident vasculaire cérébral ischémique aigu, en complément du jugement clinique fondé sur les variables cliniques et biologiques pertinentes.
- Ne nécessite pas de données de neuro-imagerie pour être calculé.
- Peut être utilisé pour ajuster sur le devenir fonctionnel dans des modèles multivariés lors d'études de recherche sur l'AVC à la phase aiguë.
- Peut servir de critère de sélection des cohortes dans les études de recherche sur l'AVC à la phase aiguë.
how_to_use.when: Patients atteints d’un accident vasculaire cérébral (AVC) ischémique aigu admis dans les 24 heures suivant le début de l’AVC.
how_to_use.pearls:
- The ASTRAL Score uses clinical characteristics and laboratory testing to predict the likelihood that a given patient with acute ischemic stroke will have a [Modified Rankin Scale](nabda:calc.modified-rankin-scale-neurologic-disability) result of 3–6 at 90 days after stroke.
- Developed to predict a dichotomous outcome, not a discrete Modified Rankin Scale score at 90 days.

- Does not predict mortality or degree of improvement from any form of rehabilitation.
- Should not be used as a surrogate for stroke severity.

next_steps.advice: - L’accident vasculaire cérébral ischémique aigu est une urgence neurologique pouvant bénéficier de traitements dépendants du temps (p. ex., tPA, thrombectomie mécanique)
next_steps.critical_actions:
- Intravenous tissue plasminogen activator (IV tPA) is the standard-of-care treatment for adult patients presenting with acute ischemic stroke within 4.5 hours of symptom onset, if no [exclusion criteria](nabda:calc.contraindications-intravenous-thrombolysis-ivt-ischemic-stroke) are met.
- Mechanical thrombectomy is the standard-of-care treatment for selected adult patients presenting with acute ischemic stroke due to LVO presenting in the acute setting.
- Note that the appropriateness of patient for endovascular intervention depends on multiple factors, such as time since onset, neuroimaging, baseline functional status, and others.
- Appropriateness for intravenous thrombolysis or mechanical thrombectomy should be determined by neurological/neurosurgical consultant whenever available.

evidence:
The ASTRAL (Acute Stroke Registry and Analysis of Lausanne) Score was originally developed in a study by[Ntaios et al](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/22649218)in 2012, which identified six clinical and laboratory predictors of poor functional outcome, defined as a [Modified Rankin Scale](nabda:calc.modified-rankin-scale-neurologic-disability) result of 3–6 at 90 days in a registry of patients with acute ischemic stroke from Lausanne, Switzerland ( *n* = 1,645).

The AUC was 0.85 in the derivation cohort; this study also had an internal validation of the score using separate stroke registry cohorts from Athens ( *n* = 1,659; AUC 0.94) and Vienna ( *n* = 653; AUC 0.77). The Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test was non-significant in all cohorts, indicating a well-calibrated score (derivation, *p* = 0.43; Athens, *p* = 0.22; Vienna, *p* = 0.49).

The ASTRAL Score was determined to have the following specificities, sensitivities, and positive and negative predictive values for determining functional outcome (mRS 3–6) at 90 days at the cut-points below. Note: Due to low numbers of observations, numbers associated with the highest ASTRAL Scores should be interpreted with caution.

| ASTRAL Score cut-point | Sensitivity, % | Specificity, % | Positive predictive value, % | Negative predictive value, % |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 18 | 97.3 | 28.5 | 40.7 | 95.4 |
| 23 | 84.8 | 65.9 | 55.6 | 89.6 |
| 31 | 59.6 | 90.2 | 75.5 | 81.6 |
| 38 | 31.3 | 97.5 | 86.5 | 73.8 |
| 43 | 17.4 | 99.6 | 96.0 | 70.5 |

The ASTRAL Score was subsequently validated by[Liu et al (2013)](https://stroke.ahajournals.org/content/44/5/1443)in a Chinese cohort ( *n* = 3,755). The AUC was comparable to that determined in the original derivation study by Ntaios et al (AUC 0.82, 95%CI, 0.81-0.83).

In the largest validation study of the ASTRAL Score to date,[Cooray et al (2016)](https://stroke.ahajournals.org/content/47/6/1493)examined the prediction of functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke treated with IV thrombolysis as part of the SITS-ISTR (Safe Implementation of Thrombolysis in Stroke-International Stroke Thrombolysis Register; *n* = 36,131). While the AUC of the ASTRAL score was 0.79 (95%CI, 0.786 – 0.795), the SITS-ISTR cohort had a higher mean NIH stroke scale (12.2 vs. 8.9, p<0.0001), a shorter time from onset to assessment (82.2 min vs. 395.8 min, p<0.0001) and a smaller proportion of patients achieving 0-2 at 90 days (57.4% vs 66%) than the original derivation cohort.

Multiple external validations have been conducted for the ASTRAL Score’s ability to predict post-stroke outcomes not examined in the original ASTRAL Score derivation study, including:

- 12-month functional outcome ([Liu 2013](https://stroke.ahajournals.org/content/44/5/1443)).
- 5-year functional outcome ([Papavasileou 2013](https://stroke.ahajournals.org/content/44/6/1616)).
- Mortality at 5 years ([Papavasileou 2013](https://stroke.ahajournals.org/content/44/6/1616)).
- In-hospital functional outcome and mortality ([Kuster 2016](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/?term=26982991)).

In addition, a recent analysis of a large independent European dataset showed that the ASTRAL Score performed best when compared to 6 similar prognostic scores, though the authors cautioned that it still may not prognosticate well enough to be used as the only basis for clinical decision making ([Quinn 2017](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/28794250)).
